settings.heading: Tips on Choosing the Right Rug: The Ultimate Guide for Different Living Spaces
Tips on choosing the right rug for different spaces:

settings.text:
1. Living Room: Anchor Your Furniture

Homeowners usually make their biggest mistake by selecting small-sized rugs which they choose to install in their living room because this space serves as the most common area for rug installation.

The "Legs On" Rule: For a cohesive look, ensure the rug is large enough so that at least the front legs of all major seating
(sofas and chairs) rest on it. The furniture arrangement creates a binding
element which enables people to identify their designated seating area.

Material Choice: If this space experiences high foot traffic, select a jute rug which offers durability or a synthetic rug with low pile for protection against daily damage.

2. Dining Room: The Chair Test

The dining room rug needs to provide sufficient functionality which supports both chair movement and unintentional spills.

The 24-Inch Rule: Measure your dining table and add at least 24 inches (60 cm) to all sides. The dining room rug maintains protection through this rule because it requires chair back legs to remain on the rug when guests take their seats.

Shape Synergy: Match the rug shape to the table. Round rugs should be used with circular dining tables while rectangular area rugs should be used with long trestle tables to achieve visual harmony.

3. Bedroom: A Soft Start to the Day

The main purpose of bedroom design creates a space that provides comfort. The floor must offer a gentle surface which you can step onto when getting out of bed.

Placement: The bed requires a large rug that must be placed horizontally underneath it to cover its bed.

Custom Solutions: Custom rugs provide the ability to create floor coverings which will match your specific room design needs when your master suite contains unique architectural elements and your fireplace occupies a corner space.

4. Kitchen and Entryway: Durability First The "high-mess" areas need rugs which possess both strength and quick cleaning abilities. The kitchen requires washable rugs which function as the
ultimate standard in flooring. The kitchen mat provides a soft surface for standing during cooking which becomes machine washable after a food accident. Round rugs in a spacious entryway create an elegant design element which directs visitors to different areas of the house.
